idea: Streamline the ralph-overview plugin install for new consumer projects. Reduce the 7 manual steps after /plugin install to zero or one operator action.

candidateDirections.name: Shared init engine with multiple surfaces (skill primary + CLI + optional MCP)
candidateDirections.summary: One shared scripts/init-consumer.mjs engine; thin /overview-init slash skill (interactive), `bin/ralph-overview.mjs init` CLI, optional overview.init MCP tool. Extends existing install-server.ts. Dry-run + refuse-to-overwrite semantics.

candidateDirections.name: Lazy auto-bootstrap (postinstall or first-run sync)
candidateDirections.summary: Zero operator action: first sync detects missing files and writes templates at default paths. Blocked on Claude Code plugin lifecycle (postinstall hook may not exist); restart still required so 'install equals done' is unreachable.

candidateDirections.name: Invest in ongoing bookkeeping skills instead of init (reframe)
candidateDirections.summary: Reframe: install happens once; task-status edits happen weekly. Build /overview-add-task, /overview-edit-task, /overview-set-status FIRST. Highest leverage per operator-hour; init friction amortizes to zero.

candidateDirections.name: Do nothing automated — INSTALL.md + post-install banner
candidateDirections.summary: Polish existing docs/installation.md + add launch.cjs first-run banner. Closes 80% of operator friction at 5% of engineering cost. Zero new code, zero failure modes, zero migration story.

candidateDirections.name: Plugin self-diagnoses on first run — helpful error + minimal CLI file-copier
candidateDirections.summary: Replace opaque missing-file errors with structured guidance: 'run init OR copy these files OR paste this MCP stanza, then restart'. CLI is a 30-line file-copier that REFUSES to overwrite. No schema knowledge, no merge logic. Dodges the 'ran-init-twice' failure mode by construction.

questionsForSynthesis: What is the net-new consumer install rate per quarter? If <4, D-004 (docs only) is strictly best; if >4, D-001 starts to amortize.
Does the Claude Code plugin lifecycle support a postinstall hook? D-002 hinges on this.
Are operators complaining about install steps themselves, or about not knowing what the steps were? Different problems.
Behavior when init runs twice on the same project — refuse, prompt, merge, or overwrite?
Is recurring bookkeeping friction (D-003) more painful than initial install (D-001)?
Should .mcp.json safe-merge be a plugin responsibility or a Claude Code host responsibility?
